input.quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only assignment provision and no change-of-control trigger appears anywhere in the document. It fails the fallback on material terms: neither party has a successor/M&A carve-out (a Client merger or sale of substantially all assets would need TrueLink's approval), there is no written-notice mechanic, and the approval standard is unqualified rather than "not unreasonably withheld". We target the preferred position with the smallest edit: the mutual approval requirement (including Client's residual consent obligation for other assignments) is retained and qualified as not unreasonably withheld, the no-approval exception is limited to Client transfers to an affiliate or transaction successor, and a short second sentence adds the competitor bar and confirms no TrueLink termination right on a Client change of control.

ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
ops.newText: Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, not to be unreasonably withheld, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment by Client to an affiliate or successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets.

ops.text: TrueLink shall never assign or transfer its rights to a competitor of Client, and a change of control of Client shall give TrueLink no right to terminate this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We kept the mutual approval requirement but made it subject to a reasonableness standard and limited the no-approval exception to Client transfers to an affiliate or transaction successor; we also barred TrueLink from assigning to a competitor of Client and confirmed a change of control of Client gives TrueLink no termination right.
proposal.summary: Keep the mutual consent restriction but qualify it as not unreasonably withheld, limit the no-approval exception to Client affiliate/successor transfers, and bar TrueLink competitor assignment and any change-of-control termination.

mappings.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
